brief.headline: Tesla's reported revenue moved down 2.9% while operating income fell 38%, with a shrinking regulatory-credit line carrying a quarter of the top-line movement, growth in energy and services offsetting most of it, and interest income supplying about a third of pre-tax income.

threads.title: What held the top line up
threads.reading: Revenue moved from $97.69B to $94.83B, a 2.9% decline. Automotive regulatory credits, 2.8% of the prior-period base, fell $0.77B and carried 26.9% of the total movement — 9.5x its weight. Two non-vehicle lines pulled the other way: energy generation and storage grew $2.71B, masking 95% of the decline, and services and other grew $2.00B, masking 70% of it. The composition of the reported number changed more than the number did.
supporting: Energy generation and storage sales grew $2.71B, offsetting 95% of the period's decline (Class A, Revenue composition check, 10-K disaggregation of revenue, R44).
Services and other grew $2.00B, offsetting 70% of the decline (Class A, Revenue composition check, R44).

The company's quarterly earnings release stating revenue of $28.2B for the period ended 2026-06-30 matched the $28.24B reported to the SEC, a 0.13% difference (Class B release, tested against Class A filings by the Management claims check).
against: Automotive regulatory credits fell $0.77B, from $2.76B to $1.99B, and accounted for 26.9% of the total revenue movement while being 2.8% of revenue (Class A, Revenue composition check, R44).
Total revenue still fell 2.9%, from $97.69B to $94.83B, after those offsets (Class A, Financial condition check, consolidated statements of operations, R5).

sources.label: 10-K disaggregation of revenue by major source (Details), filed 2026-01-29

threads.title: Where the earnings come from
threads.reading: Operating income fell 38%, from $7.08B to $4.36B, against a 2.9% move in revenue — the deterioration sits in cost structure or pricing rather than volume. Below the operating line, interest income of $1.68B was 32% of $5.28B in pre-tax income, so roughly a third of pre-tax earnings tracks rates and cash balances rather than the product business. The company's own quarterly release describes the same direction at a steeper rate.
supporting: The company disclosed the operating decline itself: the release quoted a 57% YoY drop in quarterly operating income to $0.4B and a 1.4% operating margin, and the $400M stated matched the $398M reported to the SEC within 0.50% (Class B release, tested against Class A by the Management claims check).
Interest income of $1.68B is a reported line in the consolidated statements of operations, not an estimate (Class A, Financial condition check, R5).
against: Operating income fell 38% ($7.08B to $4.36B) while revenue moved -2.9% (Class A, Financial condition check, R5).
Interest income at 32% of pre-tax income means a large share of pre-tax earnings moves with rates and cash balances rather than with demand for the product (Class A, Financial condition check, R5).

8 of the 10 management claims the review attempted were not testable against filed figures, so the release's framing beyond revenue and operating income was not verified (Class A/B, Management claims check).

threads.title: Risk language against the safety record
threads.reading: Across 38 risk factors the 2025 10-K added 2, removed 3, modified 30 and left 6 unchanged. The removed high-signal item described demand for the company's vehicles in an automotive industry that is generally competitive and cyclical; the added item recasts that dependency as demand for electric vehicles and adoption of autonomous driving solutions, and a second addition covers Bots, including Optimus, in a nascent industry. Set beside that, the safety record shows six campaigns in the 2024-2026 window out of 16 on record, and a Federal Register notice of a denied petition for a decision of inconsequential noncompliance.
supporting: The removed demand risk factor was replaced rather than dropped: the added factor restates growth as dependent on EV demand and on adoption of autonomous driving solutions (Class A, Filing language check, 10-K filed 2026-01-29).
The filing was actively revised rather than thinned — 30 of 38 risk factors modified, only 6 unchanged, and a new dependency on Bots/Optimus disclosed (Class A, Filing language check).

Federal Register notices show authorized and expanded foreign-trade-zone production activity for battery storage products in California and Texas, corroborating activity in the energy line that grew $2.71B (Class A, Federal Register, 2026-03-03 through 2026-08-03).
against: The explicit competitive-and-cyclical framing of vehicle demand was removed in a period when revenue fell 2.9% and automotive regulatory credits fell $0.77B (Class A, Filing language check plus Revenue composition check).

A risk factor on increased scrutiny and changing stakeholder expectations regarding ESG practices was removed, as was one on obligations tied to Gigafactory New York (Class A, Filing language check, 2024 10-K text).

NHTSA records six campaigns in the window, including Cybertruck brake rotor stud holes that may crack and allow a stud to separate from the wheel hub (26V255000) and a light bar that can delaminate and detach (25V170000), with 16 campaigns on record overall (Class A, NHTSA).
A Federal Register notice dated 2026-07-17 records the denial of a Tesla petition for a decision of inconsequential noncompliance (Class A, Federal Register).

threads.title: The comparison base moved
threads.reading: Two closed periods were revised after the fact in the XBRL company facts. Net income for the quarter ended 2024-06-30 was first filed at $1,478M and later filed at $1,400M, a 5.3% reduction; net income for the quarter ended 2024-03-31 was first filed at $1,129M and later filed at $1,390M, a 23.1% increase. Both revisions changed the base that year-over-year comparisons are drawn against, and neither carries a separate announcement in this material.
supporting: The revisions run in both directions — one down 5.3%, one up 23.1% — rather than uniformly in one direction (Class A, Restatements check, SEC XBRL company facts).
Of 351 reported figures on file, 0 were new to the ledger, so the review found no figures appearing without a prior filed counterpart (Class A, Restatements check).
against: Net income for the period ending 2024-06-30 was lowered from $1,478M to $1,400M in a filing dated 2025-07-24, a year after the original (Class A, Restatements check).
Net income for the period ending 2024-03-31 was raised from $1,129M to $1,390M in a filing dated 2025-04-23, a 23.1% change to a closed period (Class A, Restatements check).
A closed-period revision of this size changes every comparison drawn against that quarter, and the material contains no accompanying explanation (Class A, Restatements check).

brief.corroboration: The Class F material — news aggregator links, and in one case a community post on a social forum, which is the weakest item here and establishes nothing — carries headlines dated 2026-08-20 to 2026-08-22 reporting a vehicle recall of roughly three million cars in China over door handles and the discontinuation of the Solar Roof tile product; nothing in the filed material confirms either, and neither can be treated as established. The Federal Register notices (Class A) do corroborate two things the filings touch: battery-storage production activity in the energy line, and an interaction with the vehicle safety regulator, though they say nothing about amounts or effect.
not_checked: 8 of 10 management claims from the earnings release were not testable against filed figures; only the revenue and operating income statements could be compared.
30 of 38 risk factors were modified year over year and only a sample of the changes was surfaced, so the full extent of the rewriting is not established here.
16 recall campaigns are on record but only six fall in the 2024-2026 model-year window examined; the remainder were not detailed, and vehicle counts for any campaign are not in the material.
The Class F reports of a China recall and of the Solar Roof being discontinued have no corresponding filing in this material, so their effect on the energy line that grew $2.71B could not be checked.
The contents of the 10-Q filed 2026-07-23 and the 8-Ks in the filing feed were not examined beyond the earnings release exhibit.
Segment-level or product-level profitability was not available; the composition findings cover revenue only.
